source.title: DLM-Scope: Mechanistic Interpretability of Diffusion Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Xu Wang; Bin Jiang; Yunyang Wan; Bao-Song Yang; Lingpeng Kong; Di-Fan Zou

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates SAE reconstruction fidelity and insertion effects in diffusion language models, but it does not test the structure, predictability, scaling, or functional significance of SAE error as described in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports explained variance and changes in language-model loss when SAE reconstructions are inserted. These are related SAE measurements, but it does not compare SAE errors with random errors, analyze whether error vectors are predictable from activations, or test whether error patterns persist across SAE sizes. SAE insertion-loss findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study trains Top-K SAEs on diffusion LMs and reports explained variance and insertion-induced ΔLM loss across layers and L0. It never decomposes the error vector, predicts it linearly, compares it to random errors of equal norm, tracks per-token error across SAE sizes, or tests keeping the error term in circuits or steering. Insertion loss alone, with no random-error control, cannot show V3's pathological-error effect. The early-layer negative ΔLM loss in DLMs is a related but different finding, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that Top-K SAEs give a usable interpretability interface for DLMs, with favourable sparsity-fidelity trade-offs and early-layer insertion that can reduce cross-entropy (absent or weaker in LLMs). They add that diffusion-time steering often outperforms LLM steering, SAE feature dynamics differ across decoding orders, and base SAEs transfer to SFT except at the deepest layer.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains Top-K SAEs for diffusion language models and measures reconstruction fidelity and insertion-induced loss; it does not implement or compare the dark-matter error analyses in the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: In Dream-7B and LLaDA-8B, splicing SAE reconstructions into shallow layers at small L0 gives negative ΔLM loss (loss decreases). This is absent or much weaker in the Qwen-2.5-7B baseline, where insertion raises loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction insertion can lower the loss of diffusion language models in early layers, unlike in autoregressive LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-trained Dream SAEs inserted into Dream SFT behave nearly identically to SFT-trained SAEs at L1–L23, but give a larger ΔLM loss at L27 (Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction fidelity transfers from base to instruction-tuned DLMs except at the deepest layers.

record.problems: Insertion-induced loss is not compared with random errors of the same size. The relevant loss outcomes are primarily qualitative in the text and figures; uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were extracted: steering outcomes, feature interpretability scores, decoding-order dynamics, and base-to-SFT transfer do not measure the SAE-error properties in the claim.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation.
Per-token error norm predictability across SAE sizes; same-context failures; non-vanishing error with scale. Only L0 is swept (width fixed at 16K), and only aggregate EV is reported.
Whether reconstruction error harms loss more than random errors of the same size.
Whether the linear and nonlinear error components differ in feature content or in response to further dictionary learning.
Whether SAE-based analyses lose behaviour when the error term is dropped. Steering adds decoder atoms without any error-term ablation.
Whether dark matter shrinks with different architectures or training objectives. Only Top-K is used.

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source. Reconstruction error is treated only as an aggregate fidelity metric. The negative ΔLM loss result is a curiosity relative to V3, but it lacks a random-error control. LLaMA-3-8B results appear in the figures but are not rowed; they do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the SAE error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
Predictability of per-token error norms across SAE sizes; whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts; whether error persists with scale.
Whether reconstruction-induced loss harm exceeds that from random errors of the same size.
Whether the linear and nonlinear error components differ in feature content or dictionary-learning behavior.
Whether SAE-based circuit or steering analyses lose behavior when the error term is omitted.
Whether dark matter is mainly a training artifact or shrinks with alternative architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: Dream-7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured masked-token cross-entropy change when the residual stream at the target layer was replaced by an SAE reconstruction.
rows.value: Negative ΔLM loss at small L0 in a shallow-layer regime; SAE insertion can reduce cross-entropy loss.
rows.note: Qualitative result stated in the text; no numerical value for the loss change is given there. No same-size random-error comparison.
rows.check: Insertion ΔLM loss without a same-norm random-error baseline does not measure any version. The 'observed' state refers to the study's own DLM effect, not to a claim version.

rows.subject: LLaDA-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured masked-token denoising loss change when an SAE reconstruction was inserted at the target layer.
rows.value: Same pattern as Dream: shallow-layer regimes can have negative ΔLM loss; overly sparse SAEs tend to induce larger functional deviations in deeper layers.
rows.note: Qualitative findings are stated in Appendix C; no numerical values for individual layers or budgets are given in the text.
rows.check: Same as r1. Values are qualitative only (Fig. 7, Appendix C).

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5-7B
rows.operation_detail: Used an autoregressive LLM SAE baseline for comparison of insertion-induced loss changes.
rows.value: SAE insertion increases loss; the negative-loss effect seen in shallow Dream layers is absent or markedly weaker in the LLM baseline.
rows.note: The text describes the LLM baseline comparatively; it does not report numerical loss values here. No random-error comparison.
rows.check: This is the LLM comparator (Qwen) row. Loss increases on insertion, but there is no random-error comparison, so V3 cannot be assessed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
